author: Mark Atwood
text:
Workspace-architectural decision needed. The bead itself asks for 'a workspace-architectural decision bead to pick ONE Comparator shape and propagate'; this comment is filing-and-continuing per workspace AGENTS.md rather than autonomously committing to one of three non-equivalent policies.

Three plausible policies (verbatim from bead body):
- (A) Typed enum + Other(String) — mail's shape, best discoverability
- (B) Plain String everywhere — calendars/tasks/contacts shape, max forward-compat
- (C) Plain String + sibling prop::* const module per crate — contacts' compromise

The workspace AGENTS.md 'Filter algebra and control enums are explicitly EXCLUDED' policy says control enums MUST NOT receive Other(String). But mail-types ComparatorProperty IS already typed-enum-with-Other(String), carved out by its rustdoc on the basis that the catch-all exists only for client-side round-trip preservation, not for backend dispatch. So policy (A) is *consistent with* the workspace policy carve-out but also IS the carve-out — propagating it to siblings would require explicit per-crate rustdoc ratification of the same carve-out reasoning.

No clear agent-grade recommendation here:
- (A) is the highest-discoverability shape and has documented precedent in mail-types, but propagation would require 3 sibling type-crate breaking changes + rustdoc-justification of the round-trip-only carve-out per crate
- (B) reverts mail-types ComparatorProperty back to String — a breaking change to the most-mature crate, and loses real value (typo-protection, IDE completion) that the bead's own description acknowledges
- (C) preserves status quo divergence under a per-crate-discretion umbrella — minimal churn but admits 'no canonical answer'

This is exactly the kind of decision the workspace AGENTS.md 'When NOT to file human' rule 3 carve-out is for: 'two equally-plausible options presented without a recommendation' — and additionally is a public-API decision crossing 4+ crates.

Filing human and moving to next ready bead.
